messages:
alex: Quick sync — I'm putting together the PRD for the smart routing + fallback policy. Need alignment on tiers, regional behaviour, and 'compatible variant' rules before I send the RFC.
mordan: Sounds good. Can you call out the launch criteria up front? PMs will want clear cut "go/no-go" checks.
samira: +1. Also need to include customer-driven asks: per-tenant region pinning and explicit model-version pins.
alex: Drafting high level now. Thinking of three policy tiers: strict, balanced, and best-effort. Short notes:
  - strict: route only to exact model variant & region; fail fast if unavailable.
  - balanced: prefer exact variant/region but allow compatible variants in same region; fallback to cross-region when latency within budget.
  - best-effort: route to any compatible variant across regions; prioritize availability & cost.
devon: Can we define "compatible variant" precisely? Customers will expect deterministic behavior.
alex: Proposed definition in PRD draft:
  "compatible variant" := a model variant whose tokenization & major architecture are compatible (same tokenizer family, same context length) and whose output distribution is within an acceptable delta for the customer's eval set.
mordan: How do we operationalize the "acceptable delta" bit? Need metrics/thresholds.
qa-bot: Suggestion: use CLS/ROUGE-like score vs baseline prompt set. Thresholds: <5% relative change for critical flows, <10% for non-critical flows.
samira: Also include a KV-cache/priming warm-up note: switching variants should consider cold-cache token penalty and possibly trigger soft-warmup (small synthetic requests) before routing production traffic.
alex: Good call. I'll add acceptance criteria and tests. Early sketch of Acceptance Criteria (AC):
  AC-1: For each policy tier, routing decisions are deterministic given the same inputs and model catalog state.
  AC-2: Failover path must complete within configured SLO (default 300ms extra tail latency) and not increase 95th percentile by >10%.
  AC-3: Variant compatibility checks must return verdict in <30ms for cached queries; <150ms uncached.
  AC-4: Per-tenant region pins are respected even if it increases cost, unless tenant opt-in to cross-region fallback.
  AC-5: Rollout tests: canary at 1% traffic, rolling to 25/50/100 with automated rollback on quality regression signals.
devon: Edge cases to list explicitly:
  E1: Catalog entry incorrectly labeled as "compatible" (false positive) — action: route to canary with verification hooks before global rollout.
  E2: Region outage — follow strict -> balanced -> best-effort ordering depending on tenant policy, with clear audit trail.
  E3: Model variant with mismatched tokenizer — reject as incompatible; alert and auto-fall back to last-known-good variant.
  E4: Burst workload causes batcher overload in target region — policy should route to cheaper region with warm-cache option if within SLO.
samira: Also: cost guardrails. Customers asked for explicit spend caps per route/model. We should surface estimated per-token delta when enabling cross-region fallback.
alex: I'll include an example policy config snippet in the PRD for readability. Draft:
```
policy:
  name: "balanced-default"
  tier: "balanced"
  region_preference: ["us-west-2", "us-east-1", "eu-west-1"]
  compatible_variants: ["+quantized-v1", "+fp16-v2"]
  max_cross_region_latency_ms: 120
  cost_cap_per_1k_tokens: 0.50
  canary: 0.01
```
mordan: For rollout criteria, add post-deploy checks: latency, error-rate, generation-quality regression (<5% critical prompt failures), and cost delta (<15% expected).
qa-bot: Tests to add to CI:
  - unit: variant compatibility logic with mocked tokenizer mismatch.
  - integration: simulated region-outage, assert fallback ordering.
  - e2e: canary -> rollback flow with synthetic prompts and quality assertion.
ops-bot: Ops note: ensure routing decisions are logged with request_id and chosen_fallback_chain to make postmortem/chargeback easier.
devon: Who owns the model-compatibility verification? Research/ML should maintain heuristics & eval sets; infra owns the runtime check APIs.
alex: I'll call out ownership: Research = compatibility heuristics & evaluation thresholds; Infra = low-latency verdict service + rollout hooks; Platform = policy layer and configs.
samira: Timeline ask from sales: need a beta offering for a handful of customers in 6 weeks. That implies we prioritize "balanced" tier + canary tooling and per-tenant pins for beta.
mordan: Tradeoffs: 6 weeks means scope cut: drop automated soft-warmup and complex cross-region cost-estimation in beta. MVP must still have deterministic routing, variant verdicts, canary rollout, and audit logs.
alex: Noted. I'll mark MVP vs Post-MVP in the PRD and highlight open design items.
devon: One more edge case — model retires mid-request (model eviction). Spec should say: finish in-flight with same variant if running else fallback per tenant policy.
alex: Good catch. I'll add AC for in-flight consistency.
qa-bot: Quick acceptance test checklist for beta launch:
  - deterministic routing for 1000 replayed requests
  - canary configuration applied and observed at 1% traffic
  - fallback chain executed correctly in simulated region outage
  - logs contain request_id + chosen_chain
  - no regressions on selected customer prompt sets
samira: I'll compile the customer asks and send to alex by EOD. Alex — want me to draft the RFC after your PRD is up?
alex: Yes please. I'll share PRD draft by tomorrow noon. RFC review session: Thurs 10am. Agenda: confirm tiers, compatibility verdict API, canary/rollback hooks, and beta scope.
mordan: Adding follow-ups: sync with billing on cost-cap enforcement and with legal on cross-region data policy for pinned tenants.
alex: Thanks all. I'll post the PRD link here when ready. :thumbsup:
